comments.body:
There are two errors here: one is Int64 capability inconsistency (somehow); the other is buffer aliasing. The first one is not fatal. For the second one, we pack a lot of tensors into the same buffer:

```mlir
    func.func @forward_dispatch_4() {
      ...
      %0 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(0) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c86523904) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:2x384xf32>
      %1 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(0) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c86526976) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:30522x384xf32>
      %2 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(0) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c85737472) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:512x384xf32>
      %3 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(1) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c0) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:1x128xi64>
      %4 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(0) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c0) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:1x128xi64>
      %5 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(2) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c0) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<writeonly:1x128x384xf32>
```

In the above, `%0`, `%1`, `%2`, `%4` are all in the same buffer bound to binding slot#0. In the SPIR-V CodeGen flow, we lower all n-D buffers into 1-D runtime arrays eventually; though we still carry the element type in the runtime array. So this would mean we create two aliased SPIR-V storage buffers (`%0`/`%1`/`%2` vs `%4`) bound to slot#0. SPIRV-Cross would just translate that into two buffers at the same `buffer(n)` location as shown in the above. Metal does not support this kind of behavior. So it errors out. We have an [upstream pass](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/main/mlir/lib/Dialect/SPIRV/Transforms/UnifyAliasedResourcePass.cpp) to clean up such aliasing buffers. Right now it handles `%0`/`%1`/`%2`; it should be extended to handle `%4` too.

I've created upstream patch https://reviews.llvm.org/D127265 and https://reviews.llvm.org/D127266 to handle the resource aliasing unification cases. https://github.com/google/iree/pull/9381 pulls them in as a pull request. With it, `iree-run-module` can successfully run. Please help to verify the result is correct though. :)

Both patches are landed upstream so the specific issue mentioned here is fixed. I know we have remaining correctness issues for this still but that'd better be tracked separately. So closing this one. Feel free to file another one so we can put analysis in its own dedicated thread. :)
